title: Uniformizer cosets form a neighbourhood basis
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite field extension. Use the spectral absolute value, integer ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer and ideals $I_n=(\pi_E)^n$ of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Give $\mathcal O_E$ the subspace topology of the spectral norm. For every $x\in\mathcal O_E$, the sets $\{y:q_{n+1}(y)=q_{n+1}(x)\}$ for $n\in\mathbf N$ form a neighbourhood basis at $x$, where $q_k$ is reduction modulo $I_k$.

source.place: Clause 1, presentation of the profinite integer ring; parent lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower proof step 1.

proof.text: The chosen uniformizer generates the nonzero maximal ideal, so it is nonzero; membership in the maximal ideal gives its norm less than one. Write r for this positive norm. An element z of the integer ring belongs to the nth ideal power if and only if its norm is at most r^n: expand the principal ideal power; the forward implication uses that the multiplier has norm at most one, and the reverse divides z by the nonzero uniformizer power and uses the integer-ring membership criterion.

Equality of reductions is equivalent to membership of the difference in the ideal power, so the positive reduction fibre around x is exactly the closed metric ball of radius r^(n+1). Each is a neighbourhood of x since its radius is positive. As r^n tends to zero, every metric neighbourhood contains one of these closed balls. This proves the filter basis.

proof_origin.place: Clause 1; explicit closed-ball computation from parent step 1.

from.place: Clause 1: the profinite set of integers is the limit of its positive finite quotients.

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientExtension_integers_coset_basis (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] :
    letI := spectralNorm.normedField (Padic l) E
    ∀ x : coefficientExtensionIntegers l E,
      (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True) (fun n ↦
        {y | Ideal.Quotient.mk (coefficientExtensionIdeal l E (n + 1)) y =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (coefficientExtensionIdeal l E (n + 1)) x})
